title: The Art of Hedging in Academic Writing
text:
Hedging is the use of language to soften a claim or to signal that a statement is not fully certain. In academic writing, authors rarely present their findings as absolute facts. Instead, they often use modal verbs such as may, might, and could, together with qualifiers like apparently or to some extent. Such devices protect the writer from overstatement and invite readers to evaluate the evidence for themselves.

However, excessive hedging can weaken an argument and make a writer seem uncertain about their own findings. The skill lies in calibrating the degree of caution to the strength of the evidence. When data are robust, a confident assertion is appropriate; when they are tentative, a qualified statement is more honest. Experienced writers therefore treat stance as a deliberate choice rather than a reflex.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why do academic writers use hedging?
options: To present their findings as absolute facts
To protect themselves from overstatement and invite readers to evaluate the evidence
To avoid using modal verbs altogether

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say can happen when hedging is excessive?
options: The writer may seem uncertain about their own findings

questions.text: What can be inferred about a writer who makes a confident assertion based on tentative data?
options: The writer is being appropriately cautious
The writer may be overstating the evidence
The writer has used too many modal verbs
The writer has no interest in the findings

questions.text: Why does the passage describe stance as a deliberate choice?
options: Because all academic journals require hedging
Because writers should match their certainty to the strength of their evidence
Because modal verbs are impossible to avoid in English

vocabulary.definition: the use of softening language to show that a claim is not fully certain
a claim that goes beyond what the evidence supports
adjusting something precisely to match a particular standard

paragraph_translations: La atenuación es el uso del lenguaje para suavizar una afirmación o para indicar que un enunciado no es totalmente seguro. En la escritura académica, los autores rara vez presentan sus hallazgos como hechos absolutos. En cambio, suelen emplear verbos modales como puede, podría o pudiera, junto con calificadores como aparentemente o hasta cierto punto. Estos recursos protegen al autor de la exageración e invitan al lector a evaluar las pruebas por sí mismo.

Sin embargo, una atenuación excesiva puede debilitar un argumento y hacer que el autor parezca inseguro sobre sus propios resultados. La habilidad consiste en calibrar el grado de cautela según la solidez de las pruebas. Cuando los datos son sólidos, una afirmación categórica es apropiada; cuando son provisionales, un enunciado matizado es más honesto. Por ello, los autores experimentados tratan la postura como una decisión deliberada y no como un reflejo.
